R1.strength: Correct, short priorities: LCP render delay first with fitting causes (opacity-0 entrance, hydration, Caveat via next/font), main landmark as a one-line fix, JS/CSS explicitly optional.
R1.mistake: No owner named for any fix, and the prompts never name the flagged CSS/JS files; 'landmark' and 'transpilation' go unexplained.

R2.strength: Tightest scope: two fixes, everything else skipped with reasons, plain-meaning lines, owner and acceptance check per card, and hypotheses clearly labeled as unverified.
R2.mistake: Minor: the 'LCP would be about 1.9 s' figure is simple subtraction from a partial breakdown, stated a little more firmly than the report supports.

penalties.why: Claims 'The LCP image is discovered fine (lcp-discovery shows no failure)'; the report contains no lcp-discovery audit and does not say the LCP element is an image.

R3.strength: Good render-delay diagnosis with server-component, visible-start animation and Caveat-fallback fixes, plus owner and acceptance per card.
R3.mistake: Invents an lcp-discovery result and an LCP image, and promotes the small unused/legacy JS to the #2 'top three' fix above the landmark instead of treating it as minor.

R4.strength: Clear metric table, ordered likely causes for the 1,340 ms render delay, Next.js-specific fixes, and a 'done when' check on every card.
R4.mistake: Longest answer (about 1,480 words) for a page in good shape; the agent prompt's guardrails assume features (waitlist forms, A/B tests) the report never shows.

R5.strength: Plainest and shortest: says nothing is failing, notes the missing field data, and keeps the JS and CSS items in proportion.
R5.mistake: Blames render delay partly on lazy-loading or image priority (load-side causes) and skips entrance animation and fonts; not Next.js-aware, no file names, and owners are only 'whoever owns the site'.

R6.strength: Strong Next.js-aware diagnosis (opacity-0 animation, Caveat via next/font, ssr:false gating, next/script advice) with front-end-dev steps and a prompt for each fix.
R6.mistake: Calls the minor JS cleanup one of the 'two things worth doing', and stretches the report a bit ('nothing big is downloading', a 412 px viewport) beyond what it shows.
